holidays.name: National Crush a Can Day
holidays.description: This is a day for stomping, squishing and flattening empty aluminum cans before they go into the recycling bin. It's satisfying, and it also saves space. Put on some boots and enjoy it, but check that the can is empty and rinsed first.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance. It is usually linked to the recycling movement that grew after the first Earth Day in 1970.
holidays.funFact: Aluminum cans can be recycled over and over without losing quality. A can you recycle today could be back on a shelf as a new can in about two months.

holidays.name: National Scarf Day
holidays.description: This day honors the scarf, the accessory that can add color to an outfit, keep your neck warm, or hold your hair back. Wrap one on, knot it, drape it, or tie it to a bag to join in.
holidays.origin: Fashion brand Echo New York founded National Scarf Day in 2018 to celebrate this long-loved accessory as autumn weather arrives.
holidays.funFact: Scarves go back to ancient Egypt, where Queen Nefertiti is often shown wearing a tall, wrapped headdress. Scarves have been worn for both style and warmth for thousands of years.

holidays.name: Ancestor Appreciation Day
holidays.description: This day is for remembering the relatives whose lives led to yours. Dig into old photos, trade family stories, record a grandparent's memories, or start a family tree to learn where you come from.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to preserve their family history and genealogy.
holidays.funFact: You have about 1,024 ancestors ten generations back, if you count only one line of descent for each person. That's why even a small family tree gets big quickly.
